Michael Whatley

REP candidate for US Senate, North Carolina · Open seat

Former Republican National Committee chair; attorney and former energy lobbyist

Michael Whatley grew up in Blowing Rock and lives in Gaston County. He chaired the North Carolina Republican Party from 2019 to 2024 and the Republican National Committee from March 2024 to August 2025. With President Trump's endorsement, he won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for North Carolina's open U.S. Senate seat, his first run for elected office.

Where Whatley stands

Hurricane Helene recovery / FEMA
Says he worked with congressional leaders and the Trump administration to deliver more than $11 billion in Helene aid. As a former FEMA Review Council member, pledges to push reforms so relief reaches communities faster.
Cost of living / inflation
Proposes lowering taxes and making the Working Families Tax Cuts permanent, including the no-tax-on-Social-Security provisions, so families 'make more and keep more.' Blames Gov. Cooper's policies for higher energy, housing and health costs.
Energy, climate and data centers
Supports an 'all of the above' energy approach, including expanding refineries and domestic oil production so the U.S. does not depend on foreign oil. Says this would lower energy costs.
Immigration enforcement
Supports the Trump administration's border and enforcement actions and pledges to work on removing 'criminal illegal aliens' from North Carolina. He is endorsed by the National Border Patrol Council.
Public safety / criminal justice
Proposes rolling back cashless bail, putting more police on the street with better pay, and creating a federal version of North Carolina's Iryna's Law, which limits pretrial release.
Military spending / health care
Defended the One Big Beautiful Bill, including its Medicaid changes. Says government should get 'out of the way' in favor of market-driven solutions on health care.
Abortion
Described himself as 'the most pro-life chair in the history of the Republican Party.' Backed North Carolina's 12-week abortion limit and opposed Gov. Cooper's veto of it.
Education
Supports the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit for private school scholarships and says education dollars should follow students to public, private, charter or home schools.

Background

  • Republican nominee for U.S. Senate, North Carolina (won primary March 3, 2026)
  • Chair, Republican National Committee (March 2024–August 2025)
  • Chair, North Carolina Republican Party (2019–2024)
  • Led the Energy, Environment and Agriculture teams on the 2016 Trump presidential transition
  • Registered lobbyist, including for Consumer Energy Alliance and HBW Resources
  • Chief of staff to U.S. Sen. Elizabeth Dole (2004–2007)
  • Worked at the U.S. Department of Energy under President George W. Bush
  • Education: B.A., UNC Charlotte; master's, Wake Forest University; master's and J.D., University of Notre Dame
